parts.part: whole town (single stone-walled enclosure, about 130 by 100 m)
parts.layout_phase: Sub-period IA (mature Harappan) of Period I, by inference: the report describes the fortification without assigning it to a sub-period
parts.what_was_built: K. V. Soundara Rajan's 1963-64 excavation found 'a massive stone fortification (pl. VII) with a basal width of 4 m., and rising to an extant height of 2-5 m.', reinforced with corner towers and salients; at the north-eastern corner a mud-brick filling formed a platform between the outer and inner stone veneers. 'For the habitation inside the town, it was noticed that many houses were built against the fort-wall itself', and 'three structural phases were recognized for Sub-period I A, no such phase was determined for Sub-period I B' (IAR 1963-64, p. 11). The structures of Period II 'were found perched on the topmost extant courses of the fort-wall, which had long since ceased to be of any functional use or interest' (p. 12). Soundara Rajan later wrote that 'The citadel-complex continued in use throughout the two main cultural stages, viz. IA & IB' (Soundara Rajan 1984, p. 219), and his plan shows a rubble-stone rampart with an entrance, a cross-wall and a mud-brick revetment (fig. 25.2, p. 218). Harappan pottery occurs from the lowest level (IAR 1963-64, p. 11), so the walled town belongs to Period I and most probably to its first sub-period, IA.
parts.excavator_basis: Cross-dating: 'From a comparative study of the material it would be reasonable to assign a time range of circa 2000-1600 B.C. for Period I' (IAR 1963-64, p. 12). The range covers both sub-periods; no separate range is given for IA. Soundara Rajan later describes the Desalpur chronology as 'primarily assessed stratigraphically' and aligns it with the radiocarbon bracket of c. 2100-1700 B.C. for Surkotada (Soundara Rajan 1984, p. 218).

syntheses.statement: From a study of 108 sherds collected at the site by the Department of Archaeology, University of Kerala, Uesugi and colleagues conclude that most of the pottery 'can date to the Sorath Harappan pottery, which belongs to the Late Phase of the Harappan ceramic sequence (c. 2100-1900 BC)', that 'Further study should be done in order to determine whether the occupation at this site can date back to the Early or Middle Phase of the Harappan ceramic sequence', and that sherds of Rangpur Period IIC type show occupation continuing into the Post-Urban period.
syntheses.disagreement: The ceramic phase is narrower and somewhat earlier than the excavator's c. 2000-1600 B.C. for Period I. It dates the bulk of a surface collection, not the stratified levels in which the wall was built.

syntheses.statement: Soundara Rajan, the excavator, gives the Surkotada radiocarbon bracket of 'c. 2100-1700 B.C.' and says it 'was primarily assessed stratigraphically for Desalpur also in its earlier report (IAR 1963-64, 10-12)'.
syntheses.disagreement: Slightly earlier than his 1963-64 range of c. 2000-1600 B.C.

parts.conflicts: The report assigns no sub-period to the construction of the fortification; the IA attribution rests on the presence of Harappan pottery from the lowest level, the houses built against the wall, and Soundara Rajan's later statement that the citadel-complex was in use through IA and IB. The 1963-64 report calls the site 'this fortified town', while Soundara Rajan 1984 (p. 219) calls it a 'compact citadel or fortified complex' with 'no city-complex as such'. All available dates are ceramic or stratigraphic estimates; no radiocarbon date from Desalpur was found.

first_occupation.basis: The 3 m deposit has a protohistoric Period I, subdivided into IA (mature Harappan) and IB (late Harappan), below an early historical Period II; the range is the excavator's cross-dated range for all of Period I (IAR 1963-64, pp. 11-12). Uesugi and colleagues could not determine from surface pottery whether occupation began before the Late Phase of the Harappan ceramic sequence (c. 2100-1900 BC) (Uesugi et al. 2015, p. 204).

notes: Desalpur (Gunthli) in Nakhatrana taluka of Kachchh is a small Harappan site enclosed by a massive stone wall with corner towers, excavated in a single season in 1963-64 by K. V. Soundara Rajan of the Archaeological Survey of India. Only a short report was ever published (Uesugi et al. 2015, p. 180), so the evidence for when the wall was built is thin. The report recognises one protohistoric period with a mature Harappan sub-period IA and a late Harappan sub-period IB, three structural phases in IA, houses built against the fort wall, and early historical houses of Period II on the ruined top of the wall. We take IA as the layout phase on that basis, as an inference. The only absolute range is the excavator's c. 2000-1600 B.C. for all of Period I, from comparison of finds; a later surface-pottery study places most of the material in the Late Phase of the Harappan ceramic sequence, c. 2100-1900 BC. No radiocarbon date, no later stratified excavation and no Bayesian model were found. Chakraborty (2019, p. 65) repeats the Uesugi date for 'the Sorath phase at Desalpur'. Some sources spell the site Desalpar.
